title: The correction folded beneath the headline
body: A rubber band holds a newspaper open at its correction column. The top corner is folded under so only the first line remains visible; the paper has split along that crease.
rival_reading: An agricultural office could fold away an outdated correction while updating public advice; that does not establish that response officials concealed a failed containment effort.
gloss: A correction is partly hidden beneath a newspaper headline and held in that position.

title: The sample kept under the garden sprayer
body: An empty garden sprayer rests on an open notebook. Two pressed leaves sit between the pages; green residue begins where the bottle’s base covered the paper.
rival_reading: A government cleanup office could keep ordinary garden supplies and plant samples during an evacuation; residue on a notebook does not prove the program malfunctioned.
gloss: Pressed leaves and a residue ring connect a garden sprayer to a notebook.
